references.text: The Levites receive the tithe from the people of Israel as their inheritance for their service in the tabernacle.
The Levites shall give a tenth of the tithes they receive as an offering to the Lord.
The Israelites are to bring their tithes to the place the Lord chooses.
The commandment to tithe all the produce from the fields each year.
Every third year, the tithe is to be stored in the towns for the Levites, the foreigners, the fatherless, and the widows.
A declaration that the tithe has been given according to the Lord's command.
The Israelites bring a generous offering of firstfruits and tithes of everything to the temple.
The people commit themselves to bringing the tithe of the land to the Levites.
The tithe of grain, wine, and oil is to be stored in the temple storerooms.
All Judah brings the tithe of grain, wine, and oil into the storehouses.
The prophet urges the people to bring their tithes, even though it is framed in an ironic context.
The Lord rebukes the people for withholding the tithe and calls them to bring the full tithe into the storehouse.
Jesus mentions the tithe of mint, dill, and cumin, and affirms that the tithe should not be neglected.
Jesus rebukes the Pharisees who tithe on herbs but neglect justice and God's love.
The Pharisee in the parable boasts that he tithes on everything he earns.
Levi's sons receive tithes according to the law, and Abraham gave a tenth to Melchizedek.
